brief: Goldman's weekly cross-asset note frames five points after August, when the commodity and real asset trade ran hard, long-duration and politics-sensitive trades declined, and US momentum drew down to -5% year-to-date. Thematic and factor volatility stays high while index volatility stays contained. Elevated risk appetite and growth-shock potential cap equity upside, while valuation de-rating and scope to unwind hawkish rates pricing cap downside, so September's FOMC is the tiebreaker. Waller's comments leaned on hold and scaled back September hike pricing, after Iran escalation rallied front-end yields and hit dollar debasement trades, leaving demand for rate-sensitive basket hedges and a sector-neutral 10-year pair rather than short AI and Tech. On midterms, a Democratic majority in either chamber would help ACA-exposed equities, pressure drug makers, lift non-defense government spending and, through ratepayer politics shifting AI power costs onto datacenters, favor power infrastructure. In Europe, French Domestics face more downside if OAT-Bund spreads widen, Germany's fiscal outlook is better. The desk says watch gas, not oil: Qatari LNG misses and low storage could take Dec26 TTF toward 100 EUR/MWh.
